title: Trace isomorphism
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] (the fixed setting; $X_0$ not necessarily proper), let the field stage be $\Lambda \in \{ E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell }\}$ of the datum, and let $\Lambda _X$ be the constant sheaf with its canonical strict Weil structure. The trace map $\operatorname {tr}_X$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], in the reading of [def-pod-trace-cup-reading], is the counit of $Ra_{X!}\dashv Ra_X^!$ read through the canonical orientation $\eta _X$ of [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes], the field-stage transport of the finite orientation of [cor-pur-finite-stage-smooth-dualizing-complex] (the normalized smooth trace), and

$$
\operatorname {tr}_X:\   H_c^{2d}\bigl(X,\Lambda (d)\bigr)\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }\Lambda
$$

is an isomorphism, and so is its untwisted form (the twist elimination)

$$
\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:\   H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\xrightarrow {\  \sim \  }\Lambda (-d).
$$

For the constant sheaf on the geometrically connected $X$, the geometric Frobenius $F$ acts as the identity on $H^0(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda$ and by $q^d$ on $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda (-d)$. If $X_0$ is proper, then $H_c^{2d}=H^{2d}$ and $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H^{2d}(X,\Lambda )\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda (-d)$ is an isomorphism, with $F$ acting by $q^d$ on $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Identify the actual trace, at the stated coefficient stage. By [def-pod-conventions], $a_X$ is separated, finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, and $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Therefore [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes] gives $\eta_X:Ra_X^!\Lambda\simeq\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ and identifies the counit through $\eta_X^{-1}$ with the transported normalized integration map. Taking degree zero of that shifted map gives $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\to\Lambda$. This is exactly $\operatorname{tr}_X$ in [def-pod-trace-cup-reading]; its untwisted map is the $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ there. This identification uses no properness. The imported reference to the finite-stage orientation alone does not type at either field stage: that node has $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, whereas here the field-stage transported orientation is required.

source.place: First sentence: identify the eta_X-counit composite; correct the finite-only orientation citation at field coefficients.

proof.text: Since $X_0$ is separated, finite type and geometrically connected, the connectedness clause of [prop-cohomological-finiteness], applied over the finite coefficient field $E$, gives $H^0(X,E)\cong E$ and $F=\mathrm{id}$. No properness or smoothness is needed for that clause. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ choose the representative $E_X$ with its canonical datum. The ordinary direct image descends stagewise by [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]; the definitions [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], clause 4, then represent $R\Gamma(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ by $(E,R\Gamma(X,E))$. In the point common-stage category [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], cohomology under a transition $E\subset L$ is $H^0(-)\otimes_E L$. Thus the preceding isomorphism is represented at every later stage by $E\otimes_E L\cong L$, with operator $\mathrm{id}\otimes1=\mathrm{id}$. The common-stage Frobenius convention in [def-pod-conventions] represents the operator by this same finite-stage $F$, so $H^0(X,\Lambda)\cong\Lambda$ and $F=\mathrm{id}$ at both field stages.

source.place: Second sentence, connectedness clause; spell out the common-stage interpretation rather than apply the E-only proposition directly at Qlbar.

proof.text: Apply [cor-pod-constant-coefficients] at the given field stage and in top degree $i=2d$; its hypotheses are precisely those of the item and do not impose properness. Its top-degree clause identifies $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\cong\Lambda$ with the map induced by $\operatorname{tr}_X$, not just some isomorphism of one-dimensional spaces. Explicitly, after the identification $H^0(X,\Lambda)=\Lambda$ of Step 2, the trace-induced functional associated to $x$ is $a\mapsto a\operatorname{tr}_X(x)$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda$, with inverse $b\mapsto(a\mapsto ab)$, so the trace-induced top-degree isomorphism is the actual trace of Step 1. By [def-pod-trace-cup-reading], $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ is the untwisted form of $\operatorname{tr}_X$: it is $\operatorname{tr}_X\otimes\Lambda(-d)$ composed with the canonical isomorphisms $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\otimes\Lambda(-d)\cong H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$ (projection formula) and $\Lambda\otimes\Lambda(-d)=\Lambda(-d)$; tensoring the isomorphism $\operatorname{tr}_X$ with the line $\Lambda(-d)$ gives an isomorphism, so $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ is the untwisted top-degree isomorphism $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\cong\Lambda(-d)$ also stated by the corollary. Both requested compact-support trace maps are therefore isomorphisms.

source.place: First sentence: use the existing constant-coefficient corollary and its trace identification, then evaluate the dual of H^0 at 1.

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] to $f_0=a_{X_0}:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and $K=\Lambda_s$ with the canonical strict datum. The morphism is separated and finite type, its geometric base change is smooth of dimension $d$, and the coefficient unit is the free rank-one object in degree zero (hence has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$), so it is in $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ and the theorem applies at $E$ and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its normalized-smooth-trace square commutes. Under the trace identification of Step 1, apply the point fibre to this square and precompose with the point transport $\iota$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. The left vertical arrow is the compact-support transport of [def-pur-compact-support-transport], whose exchange is by [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], item 2, the exchange $\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}$ entering $\tau_c$; so the left side becomes $F_{c,\Lambda(d)}$ followed by the trace. By naturality of $\iota$ ([lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural], clause 2, for the morphism $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}$) the right side becomes the trace followed by $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\varphi_K)\circ\iota_K$. Taking degree-zero cohomology gives $\operatorname{tr}_X\circ F_{c,\Lambda(d)}=F_0\circ\operatorname{tr}_X$, with the operators defined in [def-pod-conventions]. By [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] at $m=0$, $F_0=\mathrm{id}_\Lambda$. Thus the twisted trace intertwines geometric Frobenius with the identity.

source.place: Frobenius sentence: supply equivariance of the normalized trace, which scalar normalization alone cannot prove.

proof.text: Untwist the equality in Step 4. The untwisted form specified in [def-pod-trace-cup-reading] cancels the Tate line in the source of $\operatorname{tr}_X$ and places its inverse line in the target. The tensor, evaluation and projection comparisons used in this cancellation are equivariant by [lem-fix-weil-operations]; hence this is an equality of maps with the canonical Weil structures, not a choice of an arbitrary vector-space identification. Consequently $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X\circ F_{c,\Lambda}=F_{-d}\circ\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$. The statement of [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] gives $F_{-d}=q^d\mathrm{id}_{\Lambda(-d)}$ for $d\geq0$ at both field stages. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(Fx)=q^d\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X(x)$ for every $x$. Since the trace is injective by Step 3 and is $\Lambda$-linear, this implies $Fx=q^dx$, as claimed.

source.place: Frobenius sentence, untwisted form: cancel the equivariant Tate line and use the scalar theorem, not the twist definition alone.

proof.text: Finally assume $X_0$ proper. Use the natural proper comparison $\kappa_M:Ra_{X!}M\simeq Ra_{X*}M$ of [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius], with $M=\Lambda_X$ and with the identity compactification required there. Let $h=H^{2d}(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_M):H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\simeq H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$. Clause 2 of that lemma gives $\tau_M\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_M=\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_{Lg_X^*M}\tau_{c,M}$. Naturality of $\kappa$ for the canonical Weil isomorphism $\theta:Lg_X^*M\simeq M$ gives $Ra_{X*}(\theta)\kappa_{Lg_X^*M}=\kappa_M Ra_{X!}(\theta)$. Applying fibre and cohomology and composing these two equalities gives $Fh=hF_c$, with $F,F_c$ as in [def-pod-conventions]. Thus the proper trace is $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X\circ h^{-1}$, by [def-pod-trace-cup-reading]. It is an isomorphism and satisfies $(\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X\circ h^{-1})F=q^d(\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X\circ h^{-1})$ by Step 5. Its injectivity gives $F=q^d$ on $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$. This establishes exactly the proper clause without imposing properness on the preceding steps.

source.place: Last sentence: proper comparison with its actual Frobenius-transport identity, valid at both field stages.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded into six steps; coefficient-stage and equivariance citation repairs

proof.text: By [cor-pod-constant-coefficients] (at $i=2d$, valid without properness), the pairing $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda(d))\times H^0(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda$ is perfect and $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda (d))\cong H^0(X,\Lambda )^\vee \cong \Lambda$, the isomorphism being the map induced by the trace, i.e. the $\eta _X$-counit composite with the normalization of [def-pur-smooth-trace], which is $\operatorname {tr}_X$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup]; its untwisting is $\operatorname {tr}^{(-d)}_X:H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$. For the Frobenius action, $H^0(X,\Lambda )\cong \Lambda$ with $F$ acting as the identity is the connectedness clause of [prop-cohomological-finiteness] (no properness needed); for the top degree, the $F$-action on $\Lambda _X(d)$ in the trace is the twist normalization $q^{-d}$, of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], so the untwisted form $\Lambda (-d)$ carries the $q^d$-action, again by [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. If $X_0$ is proper, $a_X$ is proper and [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] identifies $Ra_{X!}$ with $Ra_{X*}$ Frobenius-compatibly, so $H_c^{2d}(X,\Lambda)=H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)$ (the proper comparison of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality]) and $\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_X$ becomes the map $H^{2d}(X,\Lambda)\to\Lambda(-d)$ of [def-weil-poincare-trace-cup], still an isomorphism with $F$ acting by $q^d$.

split_report.blueprint: Steps 1 and 3 realize the opening trace-isomorphism sentence; Step 2 realizes the connectedness clause at E and Qlbar; Steps 4 and 5 realize the Frobenius sentence, supplying the missing equivariance citation; Step 6 realizes the final proper-comparison sentence. The unit proper trace assertion is a specialization; the unit point-class normalization is a separate assertion not stated by this item, so no unit realized fields are overwritten.

tool_uses.why: The generic normalized-smooth-trace equivariance theorem supplies the commuting Frobenius square; the item unit gives no replacement proof of geometric purity equivariance.
Equivariance of tensor, evaluation and projection comparisons is a generic algebraic tool for untwisting; it does not replace the duality route.
The scalar action on the coefficient Tate line is a generic normalization tool, separate from the twist definition.
The all-coefficient proper-comparison transport identity makes the proper clause Frobenius-compatible, without using the finite-only comparison corollary at field stages.
Stagewise descent of ordinary direct image is used only to interpret H^0 at Qlbar, extending the E-only connectedness clause without adding properness.
